- Whether Redwood saw a throttle/fallback event in us-west during that window

- An ETA for a postmortem (we need logs and reasons for the fallback for our auditors)

Date: 2029-10-21T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent token throttling observed during canary rollout (10/21)

Vanessa / Tom — initial findings below. Posting technical notes so we have a record before the deeper RCA.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2029-10-21T08:01:30Z — Canary pool started receiving traffic for hostgroup cg-usw2-canary-12.
- 2029-10-21T08:03:12Z — We observed a sudden burst in connection attempts; the canary autoscaler triggered additional pods but the rate limiter on the shared token-bucket (legacy gating) began returning 429s at 08:03:30Z.
- 2029-10-21T08:26:55Z — Edge routing detected increased retry amplification from client side; remediation was applied via canary rollback at 08:27:10Z.
- 2029-10-21T08:47:00Z — normal traffic patterns resumed.

Root-candidate: an under-provisioned shared token-bucket used by the canary pool combined with a regression in our routing backoff logic that reduced effective token replenishment under sustained bursts. We also saw an unrelated kernel scheduling preemption on one shard which temporarily amplified latency and retries.

Evidence attached: telemetry-20291021-0992.tar.gz (server traces, token-bucket metrics, autoscaler events). I’ve also put a curated subset in the incident folder: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/incident-0992

Next steps we recommend:
- Conduct a focused RCA to confirm whether the token-bucket policy should be made per-customer instead of per-canary-pool for high-throughput tenants like Clearline.
- Sanity-check any rollback notifications in your client-side retry logic that may have contributed to amplification.
- Prepare a short postmortem within 72 hours and propose proportional credit if we confirm SLA eligibility.

Diego
SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Confirmation of impact window and next steps (postmortem invite)

Tom — following Diego’s telemetry collection and an initial technical review, we can confirm the impact window you reported.

Confirmed impact window (UTC): 2029-10-21T08:03:12Z — 2029-10-21T08:27:10Z. During that period a token-bucket gating policy on the canary pool triggered client-visible 429 responses that affected approximately 2.8% of requests routed to that pool.

SLA / remedy note:
- Based on our SLA terms (section 3.2.1, availability and throughput), this event meets the criteria for a proportional remedy. We will calculate the credit using the mutual formula in the contract and share a draft calculation by 2029-10-24EOD.
- We will notate this incident on your account (Deal D-4821) and apply any approved credit to the next billing cycle unless you request a different disposition.

Attachments included: redwood-evidence-0992.zip (server traces, consolidated request-id mapping) and a calendar invite (postmortem-invite.ics) proposing options for a joint postmortem:
- 2029-10-24 15:00-15:45 UTC
- 2029-10-25 09:00-09:45 UTC

Please confirm which slot works for you or propose an alternate. We appreciate the rapid notification and the request IDs you provided — that made matching far faster.

Thanks again — we’ll follow up with the formal credit calculation and a short RCA document within 72 hours.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
